title: White Night
subtitle: Comrades may be united in loyalty or by other means—hatred will do.

items.text: White Night
Under the cover of night, the Zeno Cavalry Corps resumes its march toward Bereggrad.
The Gryphon Legion holds position by the main road to the city. Both armies remain on high alert.
Alone on the fields comes the slow crunch of two pairs of heavy boots.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: It must have taken some convincing, especially with Sternova. She's rarely easy to sway.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I swore it would bring peace to the Don. Sabina objected, of course. "Once a traitor, always a traitor." Her exact words.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: She's right.
Igor pulls back his sleeve. A circle of neatly inscribed symbols glows faintly on his scarred arm.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The arcane incantation customized by Zeno for every arcanist commander, preventing the misuse of arcane skills.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Never thought I'd see it again.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Your arcane skill can vanish an army in an instant. I must take precautions.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Ever cautious. Good. Though, I'm surprised you still remember how to write it.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I knew a day would come when I'd need it. I never thought it would be for this.
The commander has no desire to pursue the topic. He looks away.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Keep your promise. The Hawks are circling. They will devour me and Somme if given the chance.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I know the Foundation wants no conflict between the cavalry and me, and the Timekeeper must have promised to vouch for you. Her words will not go unheard.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Were it not for the Timekeeper's mission in Bereggrad, they would have ordered you to leave the Don immediately. No two-week buffer.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: How did you learn this?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I do not need interception to know what the Joint Committee thinks, provided their membership remains unchanged.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You're a Cossack, so they sent you here to recruit new riders. For the same reason, they do not want you stationed here in your hometown.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Don't speak like you know me, Igor. You and I are no longer brothers.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Demotion, imprisonment—no matter what they hang upon me, I will do what I must to defend my home.
Igor's eyes follow the river upstream to Bereggrad's low rooftops gleaming beneath the starry sky.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We were born and raised on this land. We both bade farewell to our families that day, leaving Bereggrad and the steppe for the cold walls of Zeno.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: On a fine day, you can make out the church spire from here.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The city is not as large as it was in 99. Back then, we could easily see the suburbs too.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Many things are different. All this will be washed away in time. Do not put too much weight on it.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But the steppe remains unchanged, and so do her people. The smell of grass and dirt is no different than at the century's end.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I still cannot trust you. Krutov is but one stain on the Don. There are many more to be blotted.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: The Golden Famine will strip the steppe bare. Her people will either starve or leave.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Most will have to live off their food stores. Some poor folk have none at all.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: What does the Foundation believe to be the cause?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: They haven't investigated. The Foundation is stretched thin. The steppe is not worth their focus.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Hah. Our best hope may be the next "Storm." If it is kind, the Don will wake as she should in the next era.
Igor lets Ivan's almost cruel joke pass.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This heat is the result of an arcane ritual.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: A ritual? Bending the weather over the entire lower Don? How can it be done?

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: Commander!
The messenger's shout cuts the conversation short.
He runs up to them and bends over, hands on his thighs as he attempts to catch his breath.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Yes?
The messenger's breathing is unsettled, not from weariness, but from sheer fear.
He turns to the Zeno rebel leader with a curious expression on his face.

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: Igor ...
He mumbles something imperceptible to himself, gradually steadying his breathing.
And the moment he straightens up, he whips out a pistol.

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: This is for Alyosha!

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Hrgh!
Igor staggers back two steps and drops to one knee.
The messenger's trembling hand throws the shot off course, denying the bullet its deadly purpose.
After a brief moment of shock, the commander lunges forward to seize the messenger's wrist.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Soldier! What do you think you're doing?
He forces the messenger's face to the ground. He tastes the dirt of his home with every word he roars.

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: Alyosha, my brother. You killed him!

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: You killed him in São Paulo!

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: Why did you do it? Because he wasn't an arcanist? Because he wouldn't help you cozy up to the Manus scum?
No one answers. Besides his struggling, the night returns to silence.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Your commanders may execute any soldier who sabotages the army's strategic goals as a traitor. This is Zeno law.
Igor rises slowly and grips the military identification tag hanging against his chest. A dent remains where the bullet struck.
He is as calm as the silent nights of the Don. He steps forward and kicks the fallen pistol away.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Let him go.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: This is my army. You have no say here.
Not far off, a few warhorses neigh. Torches quickly light up the dark like streetlights.

items.speaker: Messenger
items.text: Let go of me!
The messenger struggles free of Ivan's grasp, rolls down the slope, and vanishes into the marching column. One by one, the torches go out.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Damn it!
The commander fires several shots but hits nothing.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Father!
Igor's ever-loyal son rushes over.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Burakov, don't even think about protecting that bastard.
Igor raises a hand and turns to the commander.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I'm letting it go, and so are you.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Many of your cavalry have long served Zeno. They will protect him. Pursuing this will only undermine morale.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Nothing matters more than unity in the army. I taught you this.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Your cavalry must be united—brothers and sisters on the battlefield. This is what they are: a family.
After a few deep breaths, Ivan returns his pistol to its holster.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: The hatred of those who once trusted you, a bullet to the chest, Krutov's betrayal, a "home" soon to be aflame ...

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Remember what you have wrought, Igor.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I can never forget.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: About the ritual that caused the Golden Famine.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: It was Manus Vindictae's doing, composed of multiple rites. Their goal is to expand west. First the Don, then the Dnieper.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Soon, millions of square kilometers of land will grow no crops. All of Europe will face hunger.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: What sort of ritualist has the power to change the weather over such an area?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Remember, Ivan, our enemy is a resurrected "deity."
With Ptolemy's support, Igor makes his way down the slope.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Keep breathing.
The ritualist lifts a censer above her head. Colorful fumes spill from its veins.
They creep around the bound captive like a gaseous myriapod.

items.speaker: Captive
items.text: Urrghh ...

items.speaker: Captive
items.text: Ahh—
Krutov raises an eyebrow of contempt at the horrifying display.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Is he dead?
The ritualist gives the censer a wave. The fumes rush back inside in an instant.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: I overestimated the human's mental capacity. Next time, I won't make the same mistake.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Why not bring them to the Iceberg? Or do you aim to monopolize the fruits of the experiment?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Every glorious achievement is Hers.
The ritualist's answer is vague. Krutov waves a hand, signaling a soldier to drag the body away.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I have no time for your little experiments. My army departs for Bereggrad in two hours.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Bereggrad?
The news clearly catches her off guard.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: We will eventually conquer the city—plunder it of its wealth and vitality. But departing now, you say? There were no such orders from the Iceberg.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Starvation will be our enemy's end.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: She entrusted me an army and the power to deploy them. Now that Igor and Ivan have met, they are sure to head to Bereggrad. I must stop them.
The low growl of engines rolls in. The transport unit responsible for heavy weapons is departing.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: My army is ready. This is my chance to eliminate Igor for good.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: If you won't give me the "boon," I will take it myself.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: The loss of one rite will affect the efficacy of many others.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: If the weather cools and winter returns, our attack on the Eastern Front will be jeopardized. Our entire project will be delayed.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Your privilege has its limits, General. You and your followers will accept the trial. It is only a matter of time.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Watch your tone, Ritualist. You never asked Igor and his men to wear the mask. You have no right to ask us.
He presses his gun against the ritualist's forehead. But she doesn't flinch. She grins.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Igor is a weak, indecisive coward who doesn't dare face his true desires. I am greater than he will ever be.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Do you think a gun to the head will scare me? Death is but a return to Her embrace.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: She will resurrect all arcanists—clarify our deeds. I will die with Her name on my lips.
Krutov lowers his gun.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Monsters.
He looks on as one of Krutov's soldiers drags a fresh corpse from the camp.
For the man who is already dead, this moment feels closer to withering.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: How many more will die for this?
The soldier glances at him. Without a word, he lowers his head and walks away. Charon feels a stronger pressure closing in on him.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: They die because of you, Charon. The decision was yours.
Charon turns back.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: If joining you will teach you to respect life, then, I will do so.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But it is unclear what difference my choice will make. These people will still die by your hand, only for another cause.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I am not so deranged as the Manus. I simply value efficiency.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: If you are not one of them, if you detest their behavior, why do you work for them?

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: They work for me. These lunatics know nothing of military tactics.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: They simply point in a direction and let their entire force loose.
Krutov pauses.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: What similarity could I possibly have with them?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You both start wars, bringing destruction and bloodshed wherever you walk.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: *scoff* Our purposes are different.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It doesn't seem so different to me.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: A pity you have to go. It's rare I meet someone worth more than a few words of conversation.
Charon fails to grasp the implication behind Krutov's words. He only sees a soldier approaching with a black horse.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Andreas?

items.speaker: Andreas
items.text: Neigh ...
Before he even realizes it, he is bound with rope by the two soldiers behind him.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Why do you bind me? The ritualist has already limited my movement.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I have other plans for you.
